title: Management Accounting
description: Internal reporting that drives operational decisions. Tests break-even analysis, cost allocation, and make-vs-buy decision-making.

seo.overviewTitle: Management Accounting, Activity-Based Costing & CVP Analysis
seo.overviewBody: Management accounting provides internal cost insights to optimize product pricing and profitability. Cost accountants demonstrate skills by applying Activity-Based Costing (ABC), Marginal Costing, Break-Even Cost-Volume-Profit (CVP) analysis, and Contribution Margins.

deliverables.title: 1. Activity-Based Costing (ABC) Model
deliverables.desc: Cost allocation model (.xlsx) tracing indirect overhead costs to activity cost pools and product lines.

deliverables.title: 2. Break-Even & CVP Sensitivity Calculator
deliverables.desc: CVP spreadsheet calculating fixed costs, variable costs per unit, contribution margin, and break-even sales volume.

deliverables.title: 3. Product Line Profitability Report
deliverables.desc: Management report recommending product pricing adjustments and high-margin product push strategies.

faqs.question: How does Activity-Based Costing (ABC) differ from traditional overhead allocation?
faqs.answer: Traditional costing allocates overhead using arbitrary drivers like direct labor hours. ABC assigns overhead based on actual activities (e.g. machine setups, inspection runs) consumed by products.

faqs.question: How do you calculate the Break-Even Point in units?
faqs.answer: Break-Even Units = Total Fixed Costs / Contribution Margin per Unit (where Contribution Margin = Selling Price - Variable Cost).

faqs.question: What is Contribution Margin Ratio?
faqs.answer: Contribution Margin Ratio = (Selling Price - Variable Cost) / Selling Price, showing the percentage of sales revenue available to cover fixed costs.
